rationale: Evidence: all 60 development trials ended off track with progress between 0.11 and 0.17. Line-loss events were 1.0 in every trial, and steering oscillation was 0.11 to 0.15. The robot loses the tape early in each course and never recovers, so the controller is not tracking well enough at base_speed 1.5. Max error reached about 0.06 m, the off-track limit. The likely causes are too little phase lead at speed (sensors only 3 cm ahead of the axle, so corrections come late) and too little damping (kd 0.2). Changes: (1) base_speed 1.5 to 1.2, to reduce the lateral load in bends and give the controller time to correct. This trades some average speed, but a robot that stays on the line is worth far more than one that leaves it. (2) Move the sensor row forward from y=0.03 to y=0.05, which gives more lead so the robot reacts before it drifts. (3) kp 2.5 to 2.0, since the added lead lowers the need for a high proportional gain and reduces the overshoot that drives the oscillation. (4) kd 0.2 to 0.6, to damp the faster signal changes. ki stays at 0 to avoid windup. Geometry is otherwise unchanged, so the race isolates the effect of speed, lead and damping. Expected result: the robot should stay on the line through the s-bend and slalom, with fewer line-loss events and lower RMS error. Completion within 3 s is still uncertain, because the robot needs an average of about 1.5 m/s. The telemetry will show whether the slower speed is the limit on time or the controller is still losing the line.
